data.short_meaning: One who strives and aspires to attain nearness to Allah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root shada, which means 'to strive' or 'to aspire'. Mushaddaq signifies someone who is constantly striving and working towards attaining nearness to Allah. The name Mushaddaq carries the meaning “One who strives and aspires to attain nearness to Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mushaddaq usually hope their child will grow to embody one who strives and aspires to attain nearness to allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes a sincere and unwavering commitment to the path of Allah.
data.etymology: Mushaddaq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who strives and aspires to attain nearness to Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mushaddaq total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Mushaddaq ibn Mas'ud was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad who participated in various battles. He was known for his bravery and dedication to Islam. In the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD), Mushaddaq led a contingent of Muslim soldiers from Medina and played a crucial role in the victory over the Hawazin tribe.

historical_references.reference: Mushaddaq ibn Husayr, also known as Mushaddaq Al-Qurashi, was a poet and a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He is best known for his poem 'Layla', which is considered to be one of the earliest examples of Islamic poetry. The poem expresses the longing and devotion of the poet towards the Prophet Muhammad and the Islamic faith.
